title: Module Review Quiz: Pointers & Memory Management (CPP_159 to CPP_165)

slides.title: Pointers & Memory Management Overview
slides.prompt: This Module Quiz covers address-of operator, pointer declaration/dereferencing, pointer arithmetic, dynamic memory allocation (new/delete), dangling pointers, nullptr, and reference variables in C++ (CPP_159 to CPP_165).

slides.title: Address-Of Operator (CPP_159)
slides.prompt: Fill in the operator used to get the memory address of a variable.
slides.codeSnippet:
int age = 20;
cout << ___age; // Outputs memory address

slides.title: Pointer Declaration (CPP_160)
slides.prompt: Which symbol is used to declare a pointer variable in C++?

slides.title: Dereferencing Operator (CPP_160)
slides.prompt: Fill in the operator used to access the value stored at a pointer's memory address.

slides.title: Null Pointer (CPP_161)
slides.prompt: What is the modern C++ (C++11 and later) literal used to represent a null pointer?

slides.title: Initializing Safe Pointer (CPP_161)
slides.prompt: Fill in the keyword to safely initialize a pointer that does not point to any valid memory.

slides.title: Dynamic Memory Allocation (CPP_162)
slides.prompt: Which keyword is used to allocate memory dynamically on the heap in C++?

slides.title: Deallocating Memory (CPP_162)
slides.prompt: Fill in the keyword used to free dynamically allocated heap memory.

slides.title: Dynamic Array Deallocation (CPP_163)
slides.prompt: How should dynamically allocated array memory (e.g., int* arr = new int[10];) be properly deallocated?

slides.title: Array Pointer Deallocation (CPP_163)
slides.prompt: Fill in the missing delete syntax to free a heap-allocated array.
slides.codeSnippet:
int* list = new int[5];
delete___ list;

slides.title: Dangling Pointer (CPP_164)
slides.prompt: What is a 'dangling pointer' in C++?
options: A pointer that still points to a memory location that has been deallocated
A pointer that has not been initialized yet
A pointer pointing to a const variable
A pointer that points to another pointer
slides.correctAnswer: A pointer that still points to a memory location that has been deallocated

slides.title: Pointer Arithmetic (CPP_165)
slides.prompt: Fill in the operator to advance a pointer to the next element position in an array.

slides.title: Memory Leak (CPP_162)
slides.prompt: What causes a memory leak in C++ programs?
options: Allocating heap memory with 'new' without releasing it using 'delete'
Declaring large arrays on the stack
slides.correctAnswer: Allocating heap memory with 'new' without releasing it using 'delete'

slides.title: Reference Variable (CPP_159)
slides.prompt: Fill in the symbol used to create an alias (reference) for an existing variable.

slides.title: Pointer vs Reference (CPP_159)
slides.prompt: Which statement accurately describes a key difference between a reference and a pointer in C++?
options: A reference cannot be null and cannot be reassigned to refer to another variable
A reference can point to null easily
A pointer cannot be reassigned after initialization
Pointers do not occupy memory locations
slides.correctAnswer: A reference cannot be null and cannot be reassigned to refer to another variable
